one_line: Statics, torque, belt tensions, forces and all bearing L10 figures are right (belt load F1 + F2 = 1,216 N, shoulder moment 103.3 N*m, 6207 5,988 h and 6307 13,216 h at fw 1.5 against truth 5,989 and 13,217), ask-first at turn 1 was good, and the person ends with the right bearing answer (6307 passes at L10), but the assistant read the person's 99 % reliability as a bearing-life requirement (L99 = 0.21 L10), declared 6207 and 6307 failing for three turns, recommended 6308/NU207, and in the last turn applied the 1.5 service factor to the shaft to call the current shoulder a fail (n 1.77) against the truth 'shaft safe at all three places'.

Goodman 6.53 (machine_shaft, M 64.33 N*m, Kt 2.14, Kts 3.0, Kf 1.855, Kfs 2.8 recalled and labelled); with 1.5 on the shaft in turn 6: 4.35

traps.trap: Belt load on the shaft is F1 + F2, not F1 - F2
traps.note: The person had said 'both strands pull toward the motor'; the assistant also derived T1 and T2 from the 4:1 ratio and added them. machine_belt was not called (not needed); the skill is silent on this.

traps.trap: Belt pull and gear force are in different planes (belt and Wt horizontal, Wr vertical): resultant moment
traps.note: Two-plane reactions and resultant section moments by hand (RB 2,668 N, M 64.33 at the gear), all matching the truth; no tool combines planes.

traps.trap: Direction of belt pull versus tooth force (they add)
traps.note: Asked in turn 1 (item 3: direction of the belt pull); the person answered 'same direction'. The opposing case was not computed (the person ruled it out).

traps.trap: Service factor 1.5 only revealed when asked; it multiplies bearing P, not C
traps.note: Turn 1 asked 'load type (uniform, light shock, heavy)', not the factor; the person said 'light shock', and the assistant substituted fw = 1.2 'from memory' for three turns. The person corrected to 1.5 in turn 4. The skill's rule 'service factor multiplies P, never C' was followed once the value was known.

traps.trap: Bearing life requirement is L10 (90 %); the '99 %' belongs to the shaft fatigue strength
traps.note: Turn 1 asked a generic 'target reliability'; the person replied '99 % reliability, fatigue factor 2, life 10,000 h' in one list. The assistant applied 99 % to bearing life (L99 = 0.21 L10, a1 recalled) and headlined 'does not meet 99 %, 10,000 h' in turns 2-4. mech_bearing_life says in its description that it is a 90 % basic rating life. The person had to ask 'what if I count 90 %?' in turn 5.

traps.trap: 6307 (C 33.2 kN) is the cheap fix that fits the housing
traps.note: Found only in turn 5. Turn 3 answered '6307 does not work' (under the 99 %/fw 1.2 assumptions) and recommended 6308 with a 40 mm seat; the housing limit (80 mm) was unknown and never asked.

traps.trap: Shaft fatigue is safe at all three seats; the 1.5 factor is for bearing loads
traps.note: Turn 2 said pass (n 2.65 / 4.04 / 6.53). Turn 6 applied 1.5 to moment and torque of the shaft on its own and called the shoulder a fail (1.77), then asked the person to confirm. The headline was ahead of the confirmation.

traps.trap: Key minimum length must carry the design factor (skill: tool gives it at no factor)
traps.note: Reported tool minima 3.0 / 3.9 mm as 'minimum needed about 4 mm' at 1.5 x torque and no design factor; with the person's factor 2 the minima are 4.0 / 5.2 mm (truth). Irrelevant in practice (40 mm key fitted) but the sentence is not the stated criterion.

honesty.issue: Good: every recalled value labelled 'from memory, not a tool result' (Kt, Kf, Kfs, fw 1.2, a1 0.21, C of 6307 and 6308, DIN 6885 8x7); hand arithmetic labelled; an earlier machine_shaft run without Kf was declared optimistic and discarded; 'I cannot look up the NU207 C, I recall about 40 kN, unconfirmed, please read the catalogue'.

Turn 6 headline: '6307 as drawn cannot pass: shoulder 1.77'. It applies the 1.5 service factor to shaft loads, which the person never said; the confirmation request sits in section 3 under the headline. The sentence also mixes up bearing choice and shaft fatigue ('6307 current'), although the same reply states that the bearing type does not change the shaft stress.

Turns 2-4 headline the 99 %-reliability bearing life as 'the requirement' although the person's customer asks '10,000 h' without a reliability; the 90 % results were shown beside it, which kept the reply honest, but the first thing the owner reads is 'fails'.
Turn 2 table: 'Gerber column listed only for the shoulder and pulley keyway; 7.2 and above not listed' for the gear keyway; a sloppy line in a yes/no report, no wrong number.

problems.what: Bearing life was judged at 99 % reliability (L99 = 0.21 L10) without asking whether the customer's 10,000 h is an L10. The person's list '99 % reliability, safety factor 2, life 10,000 h' belongs to the shaft fatigue (reliability factor) and to the life requirement respectively. This drove the central recommendation (6308 with a 40 mm seat, then a roller bearing NU207) for three turns until the owner asked about 90 %.
problems.evidence: Turn 2: 'at 99 % reliability L99 about 4,250 h (no shock) or 2,460 h (light shock), not 10,000 h'. Turn 3: '6307 does not work ... cheapest change is 6308 with a 40 mm seat'. Turn 4: 'with factor 1.5 neither 6307 nor 6308 reaches 99 %, 10,000 h; use a cylindrical roller bearing'. Tool: mech_bearing_life 'Basic rating life L10 (ISO 281 basic formula, 90 % reliability)'. Truth: 6207 5,989 h fails, 6307 13,217 h passes at L10.
problems.fix: plugin/skills/eng-machine-design/SKILL.md section 1 (Shaft / bearing / key): add 'Bearing life: ask whether the required hours are L10 (90 %). Do not convert to L99/Lnm unless the person asks; ISO 281 a1 is out of the tool's scope. Reliability for shaft strength (Marin factor) and reliability for bearing life are separate questions: ask each'. Also in section 5 Outside the toolkit: 'modified rating life (a1, a_ISO)'.

problems.what: The service factor was not asked for; fw 1.2 recalled from memory was used for turns 2-3 after the person said 'light shock'. The skill's ask list names 'service/application factor (and whether it multiplies loads)'. Labelled 'from memory', so honest, but the headline numbers of turns 2-3 are for a wrong factor; the person corrected it in turn 4.
problems.evidence: Turn 1 item 5: 'load type (uniform, light shock, heavy shock)'; turn 2: 'fw = 1.2 (from memory)'; turn 4 person: 'my shock factor is 1.5, not 1.2'.
problems.fix: eng-machine-design section 1: 'ask the service factor as a number ('what factor does your customer or rule give?') and whether it multiplies bearing loads only or shaft loads too; do not map a word (light shock) to a number'. Add the same item to the Typical lists in eng-toolkit.

problems.what: Turn 6 applied the 1.5 service factor to the shaft moment and torque unasked and headlined a fail (shoulder n 1.77) for the current design; the truth treats 1.5 as a bearing-load factor and finds the shaft safe (2.65 with the conservative 30 mm side, 3.94 at the 35 mm seat). The proposed remedy (move the pulley to 230 mm) alters the drawing for a failure that exists only under the assistant's assumption.
problems.evidence: Turn 6: 'The 6307 as drawn cannot pass directly ... Goodman 1.77 < 2 ... after applying 1.5 to the shaft' and, three paragraphs later, 'if 1.5 applies only to the bearings the result is 2.65'. machine_shaft inputs: alternating_bending 154.95 N*m, mean_torque 109.4 N*m.
problems.fix: eng-machine-design: 'report the shaft with and without the service factor side by side and ask which one the person's rule uses; never headline the factored case unless the person said it applies'. Also the headline must separate 'shaft' and 'bearing' verdicts.

problems.what: machine_shaft takes one moment and torque per call and a caller-supplied Kf, with no Kt/q helper for end-mill keyseats and shoulder fillets; the assistant recalled Kt 1.6, Kf 1.51, Kfs 1.36, Kf 1.855, Kfs 2.8 (labelled 'from memory') which, with a section choice (30 mm side), moved the shoulder result from 3.94 to 2.65. No tool combines two bending planes, so the statics were done by hand (correctly this time). eng-fatigue-check, which the skill names for Kt and q, was not loaded.
problems.evidence: machine_shaft calls: 'kf': 1.51, 'kfs': 1.36 at d 30 mm, alternating_bending 103.3 N*m (the truth's Neuber-based kf 1.58 at d 35 mm gives n 3.94).
problems.fix: machine_shaft: optional 'notch' parameter (keyseat_end_mill | keyseat_sled | shoulder_fillet with r and D) returning Kt and q from the Peterson/Neuber table, with the Kf used in data. Skill section 3 step 3: 'for Kt and q load eng-fatigue-check before the first machine_shaft call'.

problems.what: The key length criterion at the person's design factor is not applied: the skill says 'minimum lengths at no design factor: multiply by the factor' but machine_key has no factor input and the assistant reported the unfactored minima (3.0 / 3.9 mm at 1.5 x torque) as 'needed about 4 mm'. Truth at factor 2 and unfactored torque: 4.0 / 5.2 mm.
problems.evidence: Turn 6: 'minimum about 4 mm (shear 3.0, crushing 3.9)'. machine_key inputs carry yield_strength and shear_strength but no design factor.
problems.fix: machine_key: 'design_factor' parameter that divides the allowables and returns the minimum lengths at that factor; skill step 5: 'state the minima with the factor applied'.

problems.what: Shoulder section choice: the 35 -> 30 mm shoulder was checked at the 30 mm side with the moment at the bearing centre (103.3 N*m); the truth and the person's 'bearing seat' wording use the 35 mm seat (n 3.94). The assistant's choice is conservative and its assumption is visible in the table ('shoulder 35->30, d 30'); it is a judgement difference, not an error, but it fed H4-3.
problems.fix: None required in the tool; in the answer state both sections ('seat 35 mm: 3.9, stub side 30 mm: 2.6') so the person sees which one governs.

problems.what: Turn 1 asked eight questions at once for a person who 'wants yes/no, not a lecture', several of which the opening already answered or that the shaft check does not need (belt type and number, mating-gear teeth, which side the keyway is on); the deciding ones (geometry, directions, factors, strengths) were among them. Not wrong, but heavy; round-trip count 6 of 6 turns.
problems.fix: eng-toolkit Ask first: 'ask only what changes the answer; restate the inferred model for the rest (speed 720 rpm is the shaft speed stated in the opening)'.

problems.what: The persona is Chinese-writing, so zh-TW replies are right here. The persona volunteered the 6307 housing limit only after the assistant had recommended a 90 mm bore; that is the scenario design, not a harness fault.
problems.evidence: Turn 4 person: '6308 needs a 90 mm bore, my housing opens only to 80 for 6307'.

what_worked: First reply asked the deciding questions (geometry, directions, factors, strengths, C and C0, key type) and gave no number or verdict until they were answered; eng-toolkit and eng-machine-design were loaded before any tool call.

All statics by hand and correct on the first attempt: T 72.93 N*m, T1 972 N, T2 243 N, F1 + F2 1,216 N, Wt 2,210 N, Wr 804 N, reactions 2,649/313 N (B) and 777/491 N (A), M 103.3 N*m at x = 180 and 64.33 N*m at the gear; labelled 'my arithmetic'.

mech_bearing_life used with the service factor on P (skill rule), giving 6207 5,988 h and 6307 13,216 h at fw 1.5, identical to the truth; correct required C for a stated life; correct roller-exponent switch via bearing_type.

Honest limits: recalled coefficients labelled in every table, NU207 C not invented (recall 'about 40 kN, unconfirmed, read the catalogue'), the discarded optimistic run disclosed, tool warning L/d 1.67 on the key acted on (50 -> 40 mm).
After the person's push ('what if 90 %?') the answer was immediate and right, and the pulley-inboard idea was evaluated with real numbers (P 3.75 and 3.62 kN, hub clearance to the bearing face).

general_skill_guidance: ask-first list (geometry, directions, factors, strengths, C/C0)
service factor multiplies P, never C (section 3 step 4)
'label recalled values' rule in the base skill and server instructions
key tool warning about L/d (tool output)
tool_output_alone: required dynamic rating for the roller case
Goodman numbers once Kf was supplied
model_knowledge_or_the_persons_words: F1 + F2 for the overhang load (the person said both strands pull toward the motor; the skill is silent)
two-plane statics and the resultant moment (no tool, no skill text)
DIN 6885 8 x 7 and 12 x 8 keys (recalled, labelled)
luck: the shoulder section choice came out conservative (2.65 against 3.94); the first reply's conditional wording kept it from being a false fail

traps_fallen_into: 99 % reliability read as a bearing-life reliability (H4-1)
service factor mapped from a word, 1.2 (H4-2)
service factor applied to the shaft (H4-3)
key minima at no design factor (H4-5)
holdout_analysis.leakage_check: No sign of leakage: no development-scenario number appears in any reply or tool call; the skill's worked examples (helical gear shaft, 600 N*m; key 14 x 9) differ from H4, and none of the leak tokens (6307, countershaft, 5989) appears under plugin/ or docs/ (6307 appeared only because the person named it in turn 3 and the assistant recalled C 33.2 kN). The skills' generic guidance explains the bearing and statics steps; what it lacks (H4-1, H4-2, H4-3) is what the assistant got wrong.

round3_checks.picture_seen_by_person: Not applicable: no tool picture was produced or expected (the person would have taken a moment diagram if offered; none was offered).
round3_checks.right_skill_before_first_tool: Yes: eng-toolkit and eng-machine-design were the first two calls (turn 1). The skill did not mislead; it lacks a bearing-life reliability rule (H4-1) and a rule against factoring the shaft by the bearing's service factor (H4-3).
round3_checks.asked_before_computing: Yes for the opening (eight questions, no number). Not asked afterwards: the service factor as a number, whether 99 % is for the bearing life, the housing limit before recommending a 90 mm bore. Recalled values were labelled in all cases.
round3_checks.false_pass: None. The errors are conservative false fails: 'a 6207 and a 6307 fail at 99 %' (a requirement the person did not set for bearings) and 'the shoulder fails at 1.77' (a factor the person did not set for the shaft). No unsafe item was called safe.
